questions.question: Where is the renowned Bhatkhande music institute located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Lucknow.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Bhatkhande Music Institute is located in **Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh,** it is one of the prominent institutions for music education in India.
 
• The institute was founded by the renowned musicologist** Pandit Vishnu Digambar Paluskar** and is named after **Pandit Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande**, a key figure in Indian classical music.
 
• It offers courses in various forms of Indian classical music, including Hindustani and Carnatic styles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chennai:**

 
 
• Chennai is often referred to as the** "Cultural Capital of India"** and is a significant hub for Carnatic music, one of the two major forms of Indian classical music.
 
• The city hosts the famous **Margazhi Festival,** a month-long celebration of classical music and dance, attracting artists from all over India and beyond.
 
• Notable institutions for music education include the **Madras Music Academy**, which has played a vital role in promoting Carnatic music.
 
• Chennai has produced numerous legendary musicians, such as **M.S. Subbulakshmi, Lata Mangeshkar, and Ilaiyaraaja**, who have made significant contributions to Indian music.
 
 
 
• **Madurai:**
 
 
• Madurai is known for its rich cultural heritage and has a strong association with** Carnatic music and traditional arts.**
 
• The city hosts several music festivals and cultural events, including the **Chittirai Thiruvizha,** which features performances by local musicians.
 
• **Thirumalai Nayakkar Palace** in Madurai often hosts cultural programs that showcase classical music and dance.
 
• The region is famous for producing talented musicians, including **S. P. Balasubrahmanyam**, a celebrated playback singer and music director.
 
 
 
• **Surat:**
 
 
• Surat is known for its vibrant music scene, particularly in **Ghazal and Sugam Sangeet (light music)**.
 
• The city hosts cultural festivals that often include performances by local artists, showcasing a blend of traditional and contemporary music.
 
• Surat has produced notable musicians and singers, contributing to the thriving music culture in Gujarat and beyond.
 
• The presence of various music schools and institutions in Surat helps in nurturing local talent and promoting musical traditions.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT about the Music of India?

options.text: Tala is a cyclic arrangement of time units.
The musical instrument Kamaicha is majorly used by the ‘Manganiar’ Community of Manipur as a popular accompaniment to their songs
A raga is believed to have started as a tribal or folk tune.
The sruti is a unit of measure or small difference between the various consecutive pitches within a grama or a scale.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Kamaicha is a traditional string instrument associated primarily with the **Manganiar community,** but it originates from **Rajasthan, not Manipur.**
 
• The Manganiar community is known for its folk music and often uses the** Kamaicha** in their performances, but the **community of Manipur **is more associated with instruments like the **pena and dholak.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tala is a cyclic arrangement of time units:**

 
 
• This statement is correct.
 
• Tala refers to the rhythmic framework used in Indian classical music, **consisting of a cycle of beats** that organizes the timing of musical phrases.
 
• Different talas have varying numbers of beats and patterns, creating a rhythmic structure that is fundamental to Indian music.
 
 
 
• **A raga is believed to have started as a tribal or folk tune:**
 
 
• This statement is correct.
 
• The concept of raga in Indian classical music** has its roots in folk melodies and tribal music,** evolving over time into the sophisticated system we recognize today.
 
• Each raga is associated with specific emotions, times of day, and seasons, and many have folklore or stories associated with them.
 
 
 
• **The sruti is a unit of measure or small difference between the various consecutive pitches within a grama or a scale:**
 
 
• This statement is correct.
 
• In Indian classical music,** sruti refers to the smallest pitch interval **recognized in the music system, which is fundamental in defining the nuances of a raga.
 
• It plays a crucial role in tuning instruments and understanding the microtones in Indian music.

questions.question: In which year did the Bhopal gas tragedy occur?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1984**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

 
• Bhopal Gas Tragedy:

 
 
• It happened on December 3, 1984.
 
• It was happened due to leakage of Methyl Isocyanate (CH3NCO) from the pesticide plant of Union Carbide (now Dow Chemicals), an MNC, in Madhya Pradesh capital Bhopal.
 
• It is estimated that about 40 tonnes of gas and other chemicals leaked from the Union Carbide factory.
 
• Methyl isocyanate is an extremely toxic gas and if its concentration in the air touches 21ppm (parts per million), it can cause death within minutes of inhaling the gas.
 
• It is one of the worst chemical disasters globally and still continues to have its ill effects on the people of the affected areas.
 
• After the tragedy, the government of India enacted a Public Liability Insurance Act (1991) that meant to provide immediate relief to victims of accidents involving hazardous industries. 
 
 
• Under the Act, an environment relief fund was set up to compensate affected people.

questions.question: Identify a carbohydrate but does not fit into the definition.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the__** Rhamnose**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• While all the listed options are carbohydrates, **rhamnose doesn't strictly adhere to the classic definition of a carbohydrate.**
 
• The** general formula for carbohydrates is (CH2O)n, where n is an integer.**
 
• Rhamnose, however, has a slightly different formula: C6H12O5.
 
• **Rhamnose** is often categorized as a non-standard sugar because it has a different structural configuration.
 
• Rhamnose is important in plant biology and can be involved in the structure of certain polysaccharides, such as rhamnogalacturonan, which is found in pectin.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sucrose**:

 
 
• A disaccharide composed of glucose and fructose.
 
• Sucrose is commonly known as table sugar and is naturally found in many plants, particularly in sugarcane and sugar beets. 
 
 
 
• **Fructose**:
 
 
• A monosaccharide (simple sugar). 
 
• Fructose is often referred to as "fruit sugar" because it is found in many fruits and honey, and it is sweeter than glucose.
 
 
 
• **Maltose**:
 
 
• A disaccharide composed of two glucose units.
 
• Maltose is commonly found in malted foods and beverages, such as malted milk and beer, and is produced during the fermentation process.

questions.question: The Himalayas' outermost range is called __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option __Shivalik__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Shivalik range

 
 
• ​The Shivalik Range, also known as the outer Himalayas, is the outermost range of the Himalayas. 
 
• It features a series of parallel or converging ranges separated by deep valleys, creating a highly dissected topography. 
 
• The Shivaliks run for 2,400 km from the Potwar Plateau to the Brahmaputra valley, with altitudes ranging from 600 to 1500 meters. 
 
• The southern slopes are steep, while the northern slopes are gentler. 
 
• The range is primarily located in India, Nepal, and Bhutan, with parts extending into Tibet, Pakistan, Afghanistan, and Central Asia.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Dhauladhar Range
 
 
• Part of the Lesser Himalayas, located in Himachal Pradesh, India.
 
• Known for its rugged terrain and snow-covered peaks.
 
 
 
• Pir Panjal Range
 
 
• Part of the Outer Himalayas (or Lower Himalayas).
 
• Stretches across Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, and northern Pakistan.
 
• Famous passes include Banihal Pass and Pir Panjal Pass.
 
• The Jammu-Srinagar railway line passes through this range via the Pir Panjal Tunnel, one of the longest tunnels in India.
 
 
 
• Kanchenjunga
 
 
• The third-highest peak in the world, with an elevation of 8,586 meters (28,169 feet).
 
• Located on the border of Sikkim (India) and Nepal.
 
• Revered by locals and considered sacred.
 
• Known for its stunning beauty and challenging climbing routes.

questions.question: Rukmini Devi Arundale is associated with which art form?

• **Rukmini Devi Arundale** was a prominent figure in Indian culture,** known primarily for her contributions to classical Indian dance, particularly Bharatanatyam. **
 
• She **established the Kalakshetra Academy in Chennai**, which is renowned worldwide for its training in Bharatanatyam and other classical arts.
 
• While she was not a professional painter, Rukmini Devi Arundale had a keen interest in art and engaged in various artistic pursuits.
 
• **She often incorporated visual elements into her dance performances, such as creating costumes and set designs**.

• Her efforts have had a significant impact on the development and popularity of Indian classical dance both nationally and internationally.

questions.question:
Consider the following:

Which of the following reasons may be considered as India's pull factors for migration?

1) Labour demand

2) Natural disaster

3) Protection of human and civil rights

4) High consumption and living standards
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1, 3, and 4,**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Migration** is the movement of either people or animals from one area to another.

 
 
• Migration can be used for the journey from one place to another or the act of movement.
 
• There are many** economic**, **social**, and **physical** reasons why people emigrate and they can usually be classified into push and pull factors.
 
• **Pull **factors “pull” people to a new home and include things like better opportunities. 
 
• Good opportunities for work, **better** **health** services, and **Higher wages** are the pull factors of migration.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **​****Higher wages** typically increase the quantity of labor supplied by workers, while potentially reducing the quantity demanded by employers.
 
• **United Nations Convention on the Protection of the Rights of All Migrant Workers and Members of Their Families:** This treaty aims to protect migrant workers' rights, ensuring their dignity and humane conditions.
 
• **Push factors** “push” people away from their homes and include things like war. Poverty is the Push factor of migration.

 Hence,** Better opportunities for work, health facilities, and higher wages are the pull factors of migration**.

questions.question:
Which of the following is/are an example of public goods?

a) Defense

b) House
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only a**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A** public good** is a commodity or a service provided to the Citizen without any intention of making a profit out of it.
 
• **Electricity** is not provided free. People pay for the service or the unit of electricity they consume.
 
• National Defence, Light House, and Public Parks are examples of Public goods as people are not charged for them by the government.
 
• Public goods are non-excludable, individuals may benefit without contributing to their provision, leading to the** "free rider problem."** This can result in underfunding and insufficient supply of these goods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Type of Goods
 Characteristics
 Examples
 
 
 
 

 **Public Goods**
 - Non-excludable

 - Non-rivalrous
 National defense, public parks, street lighting
 
 

 **Private Goods**
 - Excludable

 - Rivalrous
 Food, clothing, electronics
 
 

 **Mixed Goods**
 - Some aspects are non-excludable

 - Some aspects are rivalrous
 Education, healthcare, public transportation

questions.question: Which revolutionary organisation was established at Feroz Shah Kotla in New Delhi in 1928?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the** **__**Hindustan Socialist Republican Association.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA):**

 
 
• Hindustan Republic Association at a historic meeting in the ruins of** Ferozshah Kotla in Delhi** was converted into Hindustan Socialist Republican Association in **September 1928.**
 
• Under the leadership of **Chandra Shekhar Azad**, the name of HRA was changed to Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA).
 
• The participants included **Bhagat Singh**, Sukhdev, Bhagwaticharan Vohra from Punjab and Bejoy Kumar Sinha, Shiv Verma, and Jaidev Kapur from the United Provinces.
 
• The HSRA decided to work under a collective leadership and adopted **socialism** as its official goal.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharat Naujawan Sabha** was established in **1926** by revolutionary leaders like** Bhagat Singh** and **Sukhdev**.

 
 
• The organization aimed to awaken the **youth of India** against British colonial rule and instill revolutionary ideas, promoting socialism and the rights of workers.
 
 
 
• 
 
**Hindustan Republican Association/Army:**

 
 
• 
 
The **HRA** was founded in **October 1924** in **Kanpur** by** Ramprasad Bismil**, Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee and Sachin Sanyal, with an aim to organise an armed revolution to overthrow the colonial government and establish in its place the Federal Republic of United States of India whose basic principle would be an adult franchise.

 
 
 
 
• 
 
The **Home Rule Society** was founded in **1916** by **Bal Gangadhar Tilak **and** Annie Besant.**

 
 
• 
 
**​**The primary objective of the society was to secure self-rule for India through constitutional means.

questions.question: In addition to using the arrow keys and mouse clicks, what other method can be used to move around a table in Microsoft Word?

options.text: Right-clicking on the cell and selecting ‘Move to Next Cell’
Pressing the ‘Ctrl’ key and clicking on the cell
Using the Tab key or double-clicking on the cell
Pressing the ‘Enter’ key or using the scroll wheel

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pressing the 'Enter' key or using the scroll wheel.**__

__
 
• Pressing the** Enter key** while in a table cell typically** moves the cursor** to the next line within the same cell.
 
• When not in a table, pressing Enter creates a **new paragraph**. This is useful for formatting text and separating sections.
 
• If you need to start a new line without creating a new paragraph, you can use **Shift + Enter**. This inserts a **line break** instead of a paragraph break.
 
• The layout and functions of the Enter key were standardized with the introduction of different keyboard layouts, such as **QWERTY**, which is widely used today.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shift key** is used to select a range of continuous cells in an **MS Excel worksheet.**
 
• To select a range of cells, use the shift key in combination with any of the movement keys.
 
• You can also click and hold the left mouse button and drag through the range you want to select.
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8a16178a974a5cead2c47b730e86747fc05d693b8bfedcc60b341cc193c37730.png] 
 
• To select all the cells to the right of the** active cell **in the row, hold down Shift, Cntrl, and press the Right Arrow Key.
 
• To select all the cells below the active cell in the worksheet, hold down Shift, Cntrl, and press the Down Arrow key.
 
• To select a **single cell** simply left-click on it.
 
• **Tab key** is used to move the cell cursor from one column to next from the left to right in the MS Excel worksheet.
 
• The control key is a modifier key that, when pressed in conjunction with another key, performs a special operation in the MS Excel worksheet.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about Akbar are true?

1 He introduced the Mansabdari system.

2 He defeated and merged the state of Bijapur in his empire.

3 He made Fatehpur Sikri his capital.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** __Only 1 and 3__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Akbar introduced the** Mansabdari system** to organize the military and administration.
 
• He established **Fatehpur Sikri** as his capital but later abandoned it due to water shortages.
 
• Akbar is known for his policy of religious tolerance and founded the **Din-i-Ilahi** to promote unity among different religions.
 
• He expanded the Mughal Empire significantly through both diplomacy and warfare, including the conquest of **Gujarat** and **Bengal**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **‘Mansab**’ is an Arabic word meaning rank position or status of a person. 
 
• Mansabdari was a system in which the rank of a **government official **was determined. 
 
• Every** civil** and** military** officer was given a ‘mansab’. Different numbers which could be divided by ten were used for ranking officers.
 
• During the early reign of Akbar, the lowest grade was **ten **and the highest was **5000**. Towards the end of the reign, it was raised to **7000**.
 
• Higher Mansabs were given to **princes** and **Rajput** rulers who accepted the suzerainty of Akbar.
 
• the state of **Bijapur** was one of the most powerful states in South Asia, second to the Mughal Empire, which was conquered in **1686 **under **Aurangzeb**.

questions.question: In which of the following states is the Sanchi Stupa UNESCO world heritage site located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhya**__ __**Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Sanchi Stupa was commissioned by **Emperor Ashoka** in the **3rd** **century BCE** and is one of the oldest stone structures in India.
 
• The Stupa is known for its **hemispherical **dome that houses relics of Buddha and is surrounded by ornate gateways **(Toranas)** symbolizing love, peace, trust, and courage.
 
• **UNESCO** (United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization) was established in **1945 **to promote international collaboration in education, science, and culture.
 
• UNESCO works to preserve cultural diversity and promotes freedom of expression, with initiatives like **World Press Freedom Day** celebrated on May 3rd each year.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There are **43** **World Heritage Sites** in India. Out of these, **35** are cultural, seven are natural, and one,** Khangchendzonga National Park**, is of mixed type, listed for both cultural and natural properties.
 
• India has the sixth-most **UNESCO **site worldwide.
 
• The first sites to be listed were the **Ajanta Caves**, **Ellora Caves**, **Agra Fort**, and **Taj** **Mahal**, all of which were inscribed in the **1983** session of the **World Heritage Committee.**
 
• The** headquarters** of **UNESCO **is located in Paris, France, and it serves as a hub for international dialogue on education, science, and cultural matters.
 
• **UNESCO's Global Education Monitoring Report**: It publishes the **Global Education Monitoring** (**GEM**) Report, which tracks progress on **Sustainable Development Goal 4** (Quality Education) aimed at ensuring inclusive and equitable quality education for all by **2030**.
 
• UNESCO runs the **Man and the Biosphere** (MAB) Programme, which promotes sustainable development by recognizing Biosphere Reserves worldwide. India has several such reserves, including **Sundarbans** and **Nilgiri**.

questions.question: Which of the following persons was appointed Chairman of the Second National Judicial Pay Commission?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Justice PV Reddi**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Justice P.V. Reddi was appointed as the **Chairman of the Second National Judicial Pay Commission in 2010** to examine and recommend pay structures for judges in the higher judiciary.
 
• The Commission's primary objective was to assess the working conditions, remuneration, and **service conditions of judges**, including those in the **Supreme Court and High Courts**, to ensure adequate compensation and facilities.
 
• The Commission recommended significant **salary increases for judges**, including a proposal to enhance their salaries and pensions, addressing disparities compared to other services.
 
• The findings and recommendations of the Second National Judicial Pay Commission were crucial in **improving the morale and working conditions **of the judiciary, thus impacting the overall administration of justice in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Establishment:** The First National Judicial Pay Commission was established in 1996, and the Second NJPC was constituted in 2010.
 
• **Chairman:** The Second NJPC was chaired by Justice P.V. Reddi.
 
• The primary objective was to review and recommend pay scales, allowances, and service conditions for judges in the higher judiciary (Supreme Court and High Courts).
 
• **Salary Recommendations: **The Second NJPC recommended significant salary increases for judges, addressing disparities compared to other civil services.
 
• **Judicial Independence:** The NJPC aimed to enhance the independence of the judiciary by ensuring competitive compensation for judges.
 
• **Implementation:** The recommendations of the Second NJPC were implemented in 2016, leading to revised salary structures.
 
• **Impact on Judiciary: **The NJPC's recommendations improved the working conditions and morale of judges, thus positively impacting the administration of justice.
 
• **Pension Provisions: **The NJPC also addressed pension provisions for retired judges, ensuring financial security post-retirement.

questions.question: National Sports Day is celebrated on the birthday of _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Major Dhyan Chand**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Major Dhyan Chand **(29 August 1905 – 3 December 1979)** was an Indian field** hockey player** widely regarded as the greatest in the history of the sport.
 
• He was known for his extraordinary goal-scoring feats, in addition to earning** three Olympic gold medals, in 1928, 1932, and 1936, **during an era where India dominated field hockey.
 
• Known as The **Wizard or The Magician of hockey** for his superb ball control.
 
• The Government of India awarded Chand India's third highest civilian honor of** Padma Bhushan in 1956**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **MS Dhoni** 

 
 
• Mahendra Singh Dhoni is a former Indian international cricketer and the** captain of the Indian national team.**
 
• He was born in Ranchi, Jharkhand.
 
• He made his **ODI debut on 23 December 2004** against Bangladesh.
 
• He has been the recipient of many awards, including the **ICC ODI Player of the Year award** the** Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna award in 2007**, the **Padma Shri and the Padma Bhushan.**
 
• The Indian Territorial Army conferred the honorary rank of **Lieutenant Colonel to Mahendra Singh Dhoni on 1 November 2011.**
 
 
 
• **Kapil Dev**
 
 
• Kapil Dev is named as "**Haryana Hurricane"**.
 
• Kapil Dev started his career as a cricketer in 1975. Kapil Dev won the **1983 Cricket World Cup **in his captaincy.
 
• He was also the national cricket coach between October 1999 and August 2000. He retired in 1994.
 
• Kapil Dev is the** first player to take 200 ODI wickets.**
 
• On 11 March 2010, Dev was inducted into the **ICC Cricket Hall of Fame.**
 
 
 
• **Roop Singh**
 
 
• Roop Singh Bais was an **Indian hockey player.**
 
• He was part of the Indian field hockey team, which won gold medals for India at the 1932 and 1936 Olympic Games.
 
• He was the younger** brother of Dhyan Chand.**

questions.question: A constellation of the northern sky easily recognised by a group of five bright stars forming a slightly irregular ‘W’ is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cassiopeia**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Cassiopeia A is a **supernova** remnant.
 
• It is notable for being the brightest astronomical radio source in the sky.
 
• It is the strongest radio source in the sky outside the solar system and was one of the first radio sources to be discovered, in** 1947**.
 
• The five brightest stars of Cassiopeia – **Alpha, Beta, Gamma, Delta, and Epsilon Cassiopeiae **– form the characteristic** W-shaped** asterism.
 
• Its brightest star is Alpha Cassiopeiae or **Shedar (Arabic for “breast”).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Informatio__**

 
• **Cygnus**

 
 
• Cygnus X-1, denoted as Cyg X-1, stands as a celestial marvel in the constellation Cygnus, recognized as the first galactic X-ray source widely acknowledged as a black hole. .
 
• Its discovery in 1971 marked a pivotal moment in astrophysics, and since then, it has continued to captivate researchers worldwide.
 
• It boasts a remarkable **X-ray flux density, reaching 2.3×10⁻²³ W/(m²⋅Hz) or 2.3×10³ jansky.**
 
• Cygnus is non-reusable and is designed to burn up upon re-entry into Earth's atmosphere after delivering cargo to the ISS.
 
 
 
• **Orion**
 
 
• Orion constellation is one of the **brightest and best-known constellations in the night sky**.
 
• It lies on the celestial equator.
 
• Orion has been known since ancient times.
 
• The constellation is** also known as the Hunter,** as it is associated with one in Greek mythology.
 
• It represents the mythical hunter Orion, who is often depicted in star maps as either facing the charge of Taurus, the bull. 
 
 
 
• **Ursa Major**
 
 
• The name "**;Ursa Major"** is Latin for "**Greater Bear,**" and its mythology can be traced back to several ancient cultures.
 
• In Greek mythology, Ursa Major is associated with the nymph **Callisto**, who was transformed into a bear and placed in the sky by Zeus.
 
• Ursa Major has been recognized and represented in various ways by different cultures, including** Native American, Hindu, and Chinese traditions.**
 
• The constellation is part of the family of constellations that includes **Ursa Minor, Draco, and Boötes.**
 
• Stars in Ursa Major are relatively close to Earth, and some of them are part of the Ursa Major Moving Group, a **cluster of stars **that share a common motion through space.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2abca754ac179cbd9170148ce52c47b5f5d497efa68410190edc141a60bf5eba.png]

questions.question: On 2 March 2023, the Supreme Court delivered an order on appointments to the Election Commission. According to this order, appointments will be done under the recommendation of a committee having which of the following members?

options.text: Prime Minister, Chief Justice of India and Speaker of the Lok Sabha
Prime Minister, Leader of the opposition and Speaker of the Lok Sabha
Prime Minister, Leader of the opposition and Chief Justice of India
Prime Minister, Leader of the opposition and Chairman Rajya Sabha

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prime Minister, Leader of the opposition and Chief Justice of India**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Appointments to the Election Commission will be made by a panel of the** Prime Minister, Leader of the Opposition ( leader of the largest opposition party), and Chief Justice of India.**
 
• The court emphasized the need for an** impartial and independent Election Commission,** free from executive interference, ensuring that the process of appointments is more transparent.
 
• The judgment was aimed at strengthening the democratic framework by ensuring that those appointed to the Election Commission are unbiased and capable of** conducting free and fair elections.**
 
• This ruling is to be followed until Parliament enacts a law that provides a specific procedure for the appointment of Election Commissioners.
 
• The decision marked a significant moment in ensuring institutional integrity, drawing comparisons with similar reforms in other independent institutions like the **Central Vigilance Commission (CVC)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Election Commission of India is an **autonomous Constitutional Body** responsible for administering **Union and State election** processes in India
 
• The Election Commission of India came into force on** 25th January 1950.**
 
• **Article 324** of the Indian constitution mandates the Election Commission, to conduct elections to the **Parliament and the State Legislatures.**
 
• The Election Commission consists of a **Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners**.
 
• The **President appoints** Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners.
 
• The body administers elections to the **Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, and State Legislative Assemblies **in India, and the offices of the** President and Vice President** in the country.
 
• The secretariat of the commission is located in New Delhi.
 
• They have a fixed tenure of **six years, or up to the age of 65 years**, whichever is earlier.
 
• They enjoy the same status and receive salary and perks as available to Judges of the Supreme Court of India.
 
• The **Chief Election Commissioner **can be removed from office only through a process of** removal similar to that of a Supreme Court judge for by Parliament.**

questions.question: Which of the following states is famous for celebrating the festival of Vijaya Dashami, which marks the end of Durga Puja?

__
 
• Vijaya Dashami marks the end of Durga Puja, symbolizing the **victory of Goddess Durga** over the **buffalo demon Mahishasura**, representing the triumph of good over evil.
 
• On this day, idols of Goddess Durga are taken for immersion (Visarjan) in rivers or water bodies, signifying her return to **Mount Kailash.**
 
• Women engage in **Sindoor Khela**, smearing vermillion on each other, a significant ritual that symbolizes the** strength and blessings of the Goddess.**
 
• Large processions with **music and dance** accompany the immersion of idols, and the festival brings together people from various communities, enhancing social unity.
 
• Vijaya Dashami is a public holiday in West Bengal, with celebrations marked by family gatherings and the exchange of sweets, reflecting the festive spirit.

• NIMZs are developed to promote manufacturing and attract investment in the industrial sector, as part of the** National Manufacturing Policy, 2011.**
 
• Each NIMZ is a large industrial cluster, spread over a minimum of **5,000 hectares, with integrated infrastructure,** including **roads, water, and power supply.**

questions.question: In which year was the National Human Rights Commission established in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1993**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) was established in India on **12 October 1993** under the Protection of **Human Rights Act, 1993.**
 
• Its main purpose is to protect and promote human rights, including** civil, political, economic, social, and cultural rights** guaranteed by the Constitution and international treaties.
 
• The NHRC consists of a **chairperson (who is a retired Chief Justice of India)**, members of the judiciary, human rights experts, and representatives of minorities and marginalized groups.
 
• The NHRC investigates violations of human rights, recommends actions to the government, conducts awareness programs, and a**dvises on laws and policies** related to human rights.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) is composed of a Chairperson and other members is as follows.
 
 
• **Chairman**: A person who has been Chief Justice of the Supreme Court, or a Judge of the Supreme Court will be the chairperson of the NHRC. 
 
• **First member**: Judge of High court
 
• **Second member:** Judge of Supreme Court
 
• **Other Two members**: Persons having knowledge in the matter of Human rights
 
• Special Invitee to Statutory Full Commission - ;National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
 
• **Deemed members:** Chairpersons of the following commissions:
 
 
• National Commission for Minorities
 
• National Commission for STs
 
• National Commission for SCs
 
• National Commission for Women
 
• National Commission for Backward Classes
 
• Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities
 
• Chairperson National Commission for Protection of Child Rights.
